public_rationale: On January 28, 2026, Microsoft described its quarterly addition as nearly one gigawatt of “total capacity.” [e1] A September 11, 2026 secondary report gave about 12GW overall and about 2GW dedicated to AI. [e2] These different measures do not establish that Microsoft overstated operational AI capacity. [e1, e2] Neither item provides a matched operational comparison sufficient to establish or rule out misleading presentation across the challenged period. [e1, e2]
limitations: The evidence lacks a complete communications record for September 2025 through September 22, 2026.
No independently verified reconciliation separates total, powered and operational AI-specific capacity.
The AI-capacity estimate is secondary reporting. The evidence does not establish audience effects or deliberate concealment.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that Microsoft's communications materially overstate operational AI capacity, including through misleading presentation of total capacity.
The context identifies communications beginning in September 2025. I assess those communications through the post date.
A difference between total capacity and capacity using AI-specific chips does not by itself establish misleading communication. The surrounding disclosures and what the figures measure matter.
The surrounding allegation of deliberate misrepresentation requires evidence beyond ambiguous wording.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous statements and operational records show that Microsoft materially overstated operational AI capacity or presented aggregate figures in a demonstrably misleading way despite relevant qualifications.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently complete comparison shows that the challenged statements accurately described operational capacity and clearly distinguished aggregate capacity from AI-specific chip capacity.
